felix: quick Harbor-9B quant scan (fp16 / int8 / int6 / int4) on a mixed slice: long-summaries (N=150), multi-turn QA (N=120), short chat (N=240). headline: int6 is the practical sweet spot; int4 gives big $$ wins but reproducible detail loss on procedural tasks.

anya: can you drop a tiny scorecard + deltas? numbers pls.

felix: mini table (ROUGE-L | p50 latency@1024 | est $/1k tokens)
```
fp16 | 0.744 | 150ms | $1.00
int8 | 0.738 | 120ms | $0.68
int6 | 0.732 | 100ms | $0.56
int4 | 0.708 | 80ms  | $0.38

delta int6 vs fp16: -1.6% ROUGE-L, -33% p50, -44% cost
delta int4 vs fp16: -4.8% ROUGE-L, -47% p50, -62% cost
```

lee: where do failures show up at int4 vs int6?

felix: quick triage: int6 failures = 55% compressed reasoning steps, 30% small numeric drift, 15% tone shifts. int4 = 60% missing steps that affect correctness, 25% hallucination uptick, 15% truncation/stop issues. short chat (<64 tokens) unchanged across int8/int6.

anya: latency tails? 95/99p?

felix: 95p fp16 420ms, int6 290ms, int4 250ms. 99p fp16 780ms, int6 540ms, int4 480ms. tails tighten with lower precision (packing + lower mem).

lee: product wants routing + rollout gates we can hand to GTN.

felix: recommended routing: default harbor-9b-int6; route to harbor-9b-fp16 when input_tokens > 500 OR tag == "high_recall" OR route in ["legal","finance"]. int4 reserved for internal batch only with manual audit.

felix: rollout gates: accept int6 if ROUGE-L drop <= 2% absolute on holdout long-doc slice AND hallucination increase <= 3pp AND manual spot-check passes on 50 examples. block int4 for any high-recall route; int4 needs 72h shadow + manual review.

ci-bot: Canary created: canary/harbor-int6-2024-09-15 (traffic 3%). logs: /deploys/7007

anya: thanks — can you attach the holdout queries and a 10-example failure sample to the canary ticket? we'll present to GTN after 24h metrics.

felix: will do; filing follow-up when 24h snapshot is in.
